narrative_before: A cyberattack on Jaguar Land Rover, disclosed on 1 September 2025 (disruption from 31 August), forced the shutdown of IT systems across multiple global sites and halted vehicle production for weeks, with an estimated GBP196M quarterly cost and ~GBP1.9bn broader impact; the group 'Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters' (linked to Scattered Spider/Lapsus$/ShinyHunters) claimed responsibility. JLR 'did not disclose technical details about the incident' (SecurityAffairs), and the NCSC statement provides no attack path. Media accounts describe reconnaissance of IT/engineering staff beforehand and JLR shutting IT to prevent lateral movement, but no official or detailed public source names an entry host and a lateral hop between identified hosts.
ambiguities: JLR explicitly did not disclose technical details; no entry host or lateral hop is described in any official or detailed public source as of this research.
drop_reason: No public source describes a specific entry host AND one lateral hop between identified hosts. JLR did not disclose technical details; NCSC gave only a statement. Required entry-point-plus-hop detail is absent, so dropped per the BRIEF.
